name: Billaviz Image Scrolling
author: billaviz

sections.description:
Billaviz Image Scrolling lets you create automatic image sliders directly inside Gutenberg. Select your images from the WordPress Media Library, configure the display and animation settings, and see a live preview while editing.

Features

  • One-Shot display mode: one image visible at a time, adapting to the width of the parent Gutenberg container.
  • Strip display mode: multiple images visible at once, automatically fitted to the available container width.
  • Autoplay on/off. If navigation arrows are hidden, autoplay is enabled automatically.
  • Optional navigation arrows.
  • Optional slide indicators.
  • Fade, Slide and Zoom transitions.
  • Adjustable pause time and transition speed.
  • Optional stop on mouse hover.
  • Original, Square 1:1, Standard 4:3, Portrait 3:4, Classic 3:2, Classic Portrait 2:3, Wide 19:9 and Tall 9:16 formats.
  • Thumbnail, Medium and Full Size image quality.
  • Crop images to fit.
  • Adjustable block spacing.
  • Responsive layout.
  • The slider automatically follows the width of its Gutenberg parent container; width is not configured inside Billaviz Image Scrolling.
  • Live Gutenberg editor preview.
  • Automatic responsive multi-image carousel fitting in Strip mode based on available width, slider height, image format and spacing.

Usage

Select images using the Media Library. Use Display mode to choose One-Shot or Strip, then configure the format, image quality, crop behavior, spacing, autoplay, navigation, indicators and animation. One-Shot shows one image at a time; Strip automatically fits multiple images to the available container width.
sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins > Add New Plugin > Upload Plugin.
  2. Upload the billaviz-image-scrolling.zip file.
  3. Click Install Now and then Activate Plugin.
  4. Open a Gutenberg page or post.
  5. Add the Billaviz Image Scrolling block.
  6. Select your images and configure the settings in the Block sidebar.
sections.faq:
What is the difference between One-Shot and Strip?

One-Shot displays one image at a time and adapts it to the available container width. Strip displays multiple images at once and automatically calculates how many fit from the available width, slider height, format and spacing.

Is Billaviz Image Scrolling a native Gutenberg block?

Yes. Billaviz Image Scrolling is registered as a Gutenberg block and can be inserted directly from the WordPress block inserter.

Does Billaviz Image Scrolling require another slider plugin?

No. The plugin includes its editor controls and front-end slider behavior.

How is the slider width determined?

Billaviz Image Scrolling has no independent width setting. It follows the width supplied by its Gutenberg parent container, such as a Group or Column.

Can I use many images?

Yes. Select multiple images from the WordPress Media Library and manage the selection with Edit images.

What happens when navigation arrows are hidden?

Autoplay is enabled automatically so users can still move through the slides.

What is the difference between pause time and transition speed?

Pause time controls how long an image remains visible. Transition speed controls the duration of the visual transition.

Does cropping modify the original image?

No. Crop images to fit only changes how the image is displayed inside the selected format.

Can Billaviz Image Scrolling be used inside Groups and Columns?

Yes. It is designed to work as a standard Gutenberg block inside common Gutenberg layout blocks.
sections.changelog:
1.3.6

  • Renamed the plugin to Billaviz Image Scrolling and updated the block name and repository slug for WordPress.org review.
  • Updated plugin metadata and documentation to use the new distinctive identity.

1.3.3

  • Updated the block to Block API version 3 for WordPress iframe editor compatibility.
  • Updated repository metadata and licensing documentation for WordPress.org submission.

1.3.2

  • Updated WordPress.org compatibility metadata for the current WordPress 7.1 release line.
  • Updated internal block metadata to match the plugin release version.
  • Final pre-submission documentation and metadata cleanup.

1.3.1

  • Updated the View details documentation to fully describe One-Shot and Strip display modes.
  • Updated the FAQ to reflect the One-Shot and Strip display mode system.
  • Corrected the historical changelog version label.
  • Added GPLv2 or later license metadata.

1.3.0

  • Added One-Shot display mode for one image visible at a time.
  • Added Strip display mode for responsive multi-image layouts.
  • One-Shot adapts to the parent container width and selected image format.
  • Added dedicated One-Shot transitions for Fade, Slide and Zoom.
  • Updated the Gutenberg editor preview and controls for the two display modes.

1.2.3

  • Removed the Billaviz Image Scrolling Width setting from the Display panel.
  • Removed block-level Default, Wide and Full alignment support from Billaviz Image Scrolling.
  • Billaviz Image Scrolling now always fills the width supplied by its parent Gutenberg container.
  • Preserved automatic visible-image calculation based on real container width, slider height, image format and spacing.
  • Improved behavior when Billaviz Image Scrolling is placed inside Gutenberg Groups, Columns and other layout containers.

1.2.0

  • Reworked the multi-image carousel layout from a fixed slide count to dynamic width-based fitting.
  • Added automatic calculation of visible images from the real available width, slider height, selected format and spacing.
  • Added custom Slider height with Reset to automatic format ratio.
  • Removed block-level width/alignment controls. Billaviz Image Scrolling now follows the width of its parent Gutenberg container.
  • Improved Original format by calculating each image width from its own aspect ratio.
  • Rebuilt the editor preview and front-end carousel around a horizontal track with responsive item widths.
  • Removed the concept of a manually selected number of visible images.

1.1.4

  • Rebuilt the editor asset with a unique filename to prevent stale browser/editor caching.
  • Added working Slider height and Width controls to the Display panel.
  • Added automatic responsive calculation of visible images from available width, height, format and spacing.
  • Removed the fixed Visible images setting.
  • Added an editor readout showing the automatically calculated number of visible images.
  • Added Default, Wide and Full alignment behavior.
  • Resetting Slider height restores the selected format ratio.

1.1.3

  • Version metadata maintenance release.

1.1.1

  • Replaced the manual visible-image count with automatic responsive fitting based on available width and slider height.
  • Added multi-image carousel movement with one-image-at-a-time navigation.
  • Preserved autoplay, arrows, indicators, hover pause, spacing, image quality, crop and format settings.
  • Added multi-image support to the live Gutenberg preview.
  • Improved responsive carousel rendering.

1.1.2

  • Expanded the View details window with Description, Installation, FAQ and Changelog tabs.
  • Added detailed English documentation and minimum requirements.
  • Updated the promotional cover with fully English content.

1.0.14

  • Fixed the View details link placement so it appears only in the standard plugin meta row.

1.0.12

  • Moved View details into the standard plugin meta row, matching WordPress plugin conventions.

1.0.11

  • Improved the Plugins page View details placement.
  • Added the Billaviz Image Scrolling promotional cover to the View details popup.
  • Removed duplicate Billaviz attribution from plugin row metadata.

1.0.10

  • Added autoplay control.
  • Added navigation arrows control.
  • Added slide indicators control.
  • Added interactive arrows and indicators to the editor preview.
  • Added English interface and documentation.
  • Added a View details plugin action with an English feature and installation overview.
